attributes.attribute: much like a classical temple structure

text: A sanctuary was a Celtic ritual site. The most common forms were the nemeton, or tree grove, and the sacred water-source, such as a spring, well, or pond. Water shrines date from the La Tène period. Many sacrificed weapons and other objects have been retrieved from these ancient sites. The Celts usually worshipped in the open air. They also raised sacred buildings. Archaeologists recognise three types. The Belgic temple was built for ritual and sacrifice and held rich hoards of jewellery, weapons, and metal objects. The Viereckschanzen was a rectangular building like the Belgic temple but held no sacrificial goods. The Celto-Ligurian site was rare. It came from Roman influence and looked like a classical temple structure.
objective: Document the forms of Celtic sanctuary.
key_results: Record the nemeton and sacred water-source as the common forms.
Record the three known types of sacred buildings.
Note the La Tène-period origin of water shrines.
